summary: Defined a standard-library JWT authentication architecture and delegated non-overlapping schema, API, and UI implementation work.

new_tasks.title: Update database.py with users storage, PBKDF2 password-hash fields, and task user ownership needed for authenticated task isolation.
Update server.py with register/login routes, HS256 JWT creation/verification, Bearer authentication, and per-user task authorization.
Update static/index.html with register/login controls, session-scoped token handling, authenticated task API calls, and signed-out UI state.

messages.content: Schema contract: users need an integer id, unique normalized username, password_hash, password_salt, and created_at. Tasks need an owning user_id; legacy tasks with no owner must not be returned by authenticated task queries.

API contract: POST /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login accept username/password and return a short-lived HS256 JWT. All /api/tasks routes require Authorization: Bearer <token> and scope every query/mutation to the JWT subject.

Use POST /api/auth/register and /api/auth/login, retain the returned token in sessionStorage only, send it as an Authorization Bearer token for every task request, and return users to the auth screen on 401.

decisions: Use Python standard-library hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with a random per-user salt for password storage; never store plaintext passwords.
Implement compact JWTs with base64url JSON, HS256 HMAC signatures, and constant-time signature comparison. Require sub, iat, and exp claims; reject malformed, expired, or wrong-algorithm tokens.
Load the JWT signing secret from an environment variable at server startup and do not hard-code it or return it in API responses.
Register/login are public POST routes; every task route requires a Bearer token and uses its subject to enforce task ownership.
Keep the frontend as one static HTML file and hold the access token in sessionStorage rather than persistent localStorage.
